author: Jessica Maldonado
title: New specialty pharmacy opens in Roanoke to aid seniors - NewsBreak
text:
By Jessica Maldonado ,
1 hours ago
ROANOKE, VA. ( WFXR ) – Unlike a neighborhood pharmacy, you won’t find customers walking in to pick up prescriptions at SpecialtyRX.
As the Roanoke Valley faces an ongoing pharmacy crisis and a growing senior population, SpecialtyRX says its new regional pharmacy is focused on ensuring residents receive medications accurately, safely and on time.
The pharmacy fills, packages and delivers medications to residents living in skilled nursing facilities, assisted living communities and memory care centers.
“Health care is a very local thing. At the end of the day, we need to make sure that our patients and residents have access and have the ability to get clinical insights from folks that are on the ground,” said Raghav Dubey, Executive Vice President at SpecialtyRX.
Local pharmacies face challenges with underpaid prescriptions The new Roanoke pharmacy at 811 Connecticut Ave. NE is the company’s 15th regional location.
It will provide 24/7 pharmacist support, emergency medication delivery, same day IV services and technology that allows facilities to securely track prescriptions.
“We have technology and emergency kits, automated dispensing machines at the facility level. If there is, a weather event, they can access their medications through that cabinet without waiting on the delivery from the pharmacy as well,” said Kyrillos Elsobky, Director of Operations at SpecialtyRX.
The company is an independent pharmacy and says it also works to control costs by negotiating directly with wholesalers to secure better pricing.
Currently, it has a team of 20 local employees and plans to expand.
“We really intend to be three or four times the size in the next couple of years,” said Dubey.
The company says it’s opening in Roanoke because the region has a growing senior population and an increasing need for dependable long-term pharmacy services. City leaders say this pharmacy will make the City of Roanoke a stronger destination where people can age in place.
SpecialtyRX says the company is starting with 1,500 patients and expects to grow to 10,000 patients over the next two years.
